see.b: A famous beach swim in the first week of January when the temperature is around 0°C. Hundreds of brave participants compete the cold in the sea. This event has run annually at the Choseon Beach Hotel since 1988.
Busan has been holding an annual Rock festival for 12 years now in August. Mostly Korean and Asian rock bands although some Western bands do appear.
An art festival held on the beach every year from mid-September to mid-October.
Haeundae has the largest leisure marina in Korea located about 10 minutes away from the beach walking in the direction of the Chosun Beach Hotel.

It is a great place to train. It has a wide range of cardio equipment, free weights (dumbbells up to 45 kg (100 lb)) and machines as well as golf practice facilities. It is located on the 5th floor of the Milligore Shopping Center in…
An expat rugby club open to all residents of Busan and surrounding provinces. They play mainly 10's rugby and compete in the Korean Expat Rugby League (KERA). No previous experience required.

One of the most popular summer destinations in South Korea. Haeundae beach attracts tourists from all around the country and gets really overcrowded in late July and early August. Deck chairs and parasols are available to rent for…

This is the largest aquarium in Korea with great facilities and excellent displays. There is also a 3D ride that is worth checking out. There are larger aquariums in Asia, and outside the facility looks rather underwhelming, but inside…

see.a: Haeundae Beach, next to Westin Hotel
see.b: Dongbaekseom is not a real island, but a forested area with Camellia and pine trees past the Westin hotel. It offers a pleasant and short coastal walk, and the APEC Conference Center (with great views of the Gwangali area in Busan) can…

This is regarded as Busan's 'romantic road', and climbs a hill overlooking the sea. It is often called the Montmartre of Busan by locals, although the two locations only share the attributes of being romantic and on a hill. The majority…
This is a nice forested walk along the sea coast on Dalmaji Hill with an impressive lookout in the middle. At night time the path is lit up.

Contains three art galleries of modern art (one being for children). You can probably feel pretty good about spending 2-3 hours here and feel like you've seen it all. Closed every Monday and January 1st. In case Monday is a national…

The Busan International Film Festival has had this impressive open cinema built for the October 2011 festival. Go at night time to appreciate the light show displayed on the ceiling. To get there take the subway/bus to Centum City. The…

Further along the coast, Songjeong is a 1.2km-long stretch of golden sand in a sheltered cove. There are many hotels and restaurants directly on the beach or within an easy walk. Since it is less crowded, this beach is a better option…

This remarkable Buddhist temple complex is situated on top of a large rock along the ocean. Since most Korean temples are in the mountains this is an unusual location with sweeping ocean views. You need to walk through a market from the…
Buddhist temple and monastery located up Jangsan mountain. Good scenic views over Haeundae.

Although not particularly remarkable compared to Heaundae and Songjeong beaches on eigher side, this village is remote and away from the crowds with some cafes and restaurants by the sea. You can walk here either along the Moontan Road…
Museum of Korean traditional art.
Art gallery with exhibitions of works by Korean and international artists. Lovely views over the Korea Strait.

Part of the Shinsigae mall, this spa is probably the most friendly/accessible spa for foreigners in Busan. It is directly on the Centum City subway station, making it very easy to get to. Signs and an Instruction leaflet are also…

This boat trip starts off at Haeundae’s Mipo Ferry Terminal and heads towards Oryuk-do Islets and the Igidae area. The shores of Igidae are composed of breathtaking views of fantastically shaped cliffs. This 1-hour boat trip offers…

Typically runs the first 10 days every year in October. It takes place all across Busan showcasing many international films and often some significant premieres of new Korean films. Most of the events are held on Haeundae beach where…

BEXCO is a large exhibition center with many halls, and although most of the events are rather dry (i.e. Industrial Marine technology) there may be something of interest whilst you're in town such as computer gaming or coffee making…

If you are near Haeundae, then Jangsan mountain can provide a good day's hiking. There are military bases at the summit complete with minefields (Clearly marked and fenced off), and great views over Busan and on a clear day to Japan. A…
An old mainline trainline has been repurposed into two types of tourist train - a 'sky capsule' (an elevated small tram) as well a coastal train.

A yachting club with a variety of boats for the public to try out, including tours with a yacht (₩60,000+), a dash around the harbor on a jet boat (₩40,000), Glass bottom boat (₩60,000) and jet skis (₩250,000+)
Korean sauna with separate levels for men and women. Very nice water and views over Haeundae beach. Somewhat out of the way, but if you are visiting Dalmaji road anyway then worth visiting.
Provides trips around Gwangan Bridge and beach in the neighboring area.

Best experienced at night when the impressive Gwangan Grand Bridge is illuminated. The area is similar to Haeundae but smaller and less upscale. There are plenty of local restaurants, bars and shops in the area. In summer the crowds are…

Driving (or taking the bus) across Gwangan Bridge is a great way to see the view, especially at nighttime. Viewed from the town it has an impressive light display at night. It featured in the Marvel movie 'Black Panther'.
Here is a park where people can see Gwangan grand bridge and Gwangalli beach.

This mountain offers one of the best panoramic views of Busan, including Gwangalli Beach, the Gwangan Grand Bridge, and the cityscape. The view is especially breathtaking at night. The peak features an observation deck and a beacon fire…

A unique cultural complex built in a former wire factory. It features a popular bookstore (Yes24), a local brewery (Praha Pub), a Starbucks, and various exhibition spaces. A great place to relax and enjoy the modern, artistic atmosphere.
A community hub that hosts various performances, exhibitions, and cultural classes. It's a great place to experience local arts and culture.
A famous street lined with cherry blossom trees, creating a beautiful pink canopy in the spring. It's one of Busan's most popular spots for enjoying the cherry blossom season.
A unique restaurant known for its seafood dishes and lively atmosphere. It offers a great view of the beach and bridge, making it a popular spot for both locals and tourists.
Suyeong History Park preserves the remains of the former Suyeong-eupseong fortress from the Joseon Dynasty. Informational signs explain the historical significance of the site.
A local market offering fresh produce, street food, and daily necessities. It provides insight into everyday life in Suyeong and is popular with residents.
A well-known Catholic church in the Namcheon area, recognized for its architecture and role as a local religious center.
A paved cycling and walking route along the Suyeong River, frequently used by locals for exercise and commuting.
A temporary night market operating during peak tourist seasons, featuring street food, snacks, and small craft vendors along the beachfront.
A small urban regeneration project featuring murals and street art painted on residential walls, offering casual photo opportunities and quiet walks.
An open beachfront space used for public performances, cultural events, and seasonal festivals. Visitors may encounter street performances or small-scale concerts depending on the event schedule.
A neighborhood public space used for small exhibitions, community events, and outdoor gatherings. Primarily serves residents but is accessible to visitors.
A public cultural venue hosting exhibitions, performances, and local cultural events that are open to residents and visitors.
Archaeological remains marking the original gate location of Suyeong-eupseong, with signage explaining its historical role during the Joseon period.
A designated area offering seasonal marine leisure activities such as kayaking and paddleboarding, popular with visitors during summer months.
A small cluster of ceramic studios and craft shops known among visitors interested in local arts and handmade goods.

Namcheon Beach Park is a scenic coastal park located at the edge of Gwangalli Beach. It is widely considered the best vantage point to view the Gwangan Bridge (Diamond Bridge) up close from a front-facing angle. The park features a…

A raw fish festival held annually in October. The event, which takes place on the sandy expanse of Gwangalli Beach, is a lively celebration of Busan's seafood culture. Visitors can participate in a variety of activities, including…

The Busan Fireworks Festival takes place every October along Gwangalli Beach, transforming the city's iconic shoreline into a dazzling spectacle of light and sound. Drawing millions of spectators each year, it stands as one of South…

Each year, the Gwangan Bridge is opened to the public for a walking festival. This unique event allows you to walk or run across Busan’s most famous landmark, an opportunity not available at any other time of the year. The walk offers…
A traditional fishing culture festival recreating Joseon-era coastal life with performances, seafood events, and hands-on cultural programs for visitors.
Seasonal outdoor yoga sessions organized along Gwangalli Beach, open to visitors looking for wellness-focused seaside activities.
Temporary street markets featuring local food, crafts, and small performances, occasionally organized during seasonal events.
A designated beachfront zone where digital lighting and media installations are periodically displayed, creating a modern night-time atmosphere for visitors.

Gwangalli Beach is a hub for water sports, with stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) being the most popular activity. You can easily rent equipment and get lessons from one of the many rental shops along the beach. Paddle out onto the calm…

Take a leisurely cruise along the Suyeonggang River, which flows through the heart of the district. The tour offers a different perspective of Suyeong's scenic beauty, passing by the APEC Naru Park and under a series of beautiful…

As the sun sets, Gwangalli Beach transforms into an outdoor stage for talented buskers. You can find musicians, dancers, and artists performing along the boardwalk, creating a lively and energetic atmosphere. The busking culture is a…

A must-see attraction on Gwangalli Beach is the spectacular M-Drone Show. Every Saturday, hundreds of synchronized drones light up the night sky, creating intricate shapes and animations above the Gwangan Bridge. The show features a…

For a more active and scenic experience, rent a bike and cycle along the well-maintained paths of the Suyeonggang River. The path offers a peaceful escape from the crowded beach area, with beautiful views of the river, lush greenery,…

The streets facing Gwangalli Beach are lined with a diverse selection of cafes, each offering a unique atmosphere and, most importantly, a prime view of the ocean and bridge. From trendy, minimalist cafes to cozy, themed spots, there's…

This pleasant little park is home to Busan's one true tourist attraction, the 118-meter-tall Busan Tower. This is the fourth tallest tower in South Korea, although it is over 100 meters shorter than the Namsan Tower in Seoul. There are…

A few streets of a grubby district have been 'restored' to their condition in the post-Korean War 1960s, with wooden lamppost and bronze figures illustrating scenes of hardscrabble street life. Also easy walking distance to Yongdusan Park.

This is possibly Korea's most famous fish market with a large selection of seafood there. You will have to opportunity to eat squid that is still wriggling when you eat it! Try to come very early to see the activity around the fish…

This building housing the Busan Modern History Museum was used as the Busan Branch of the Oriental Development Company during the Japanese occupation and as the Busan USIS Cultural Center (a CIA post) following the Korean war. The…

As a symbolic location for the Busan International Film Festival, BIFF Square features handprints of famous film directors and actors. Once a district with a high concentration of theaters, it is now a representative street food…

Songdo beach was apparently the first official beach in Korea and the main attraction in Busan for many years until Haeundae became the main tourist center. Today the beach is small (450 meters) and quiet with some charm, surrounded by…

Gamcheon village was a Korean war refugee camp, and backwater outside of the city center. In 2008 it attracted the attention of local university students who began painting murals throughout the village as part of their social service…

see.n: Busan Air Cruise (Songdo Marine Cable Car)
see.b: This marine cable car connects Songdo Beach to Amnam Park. It offers spectacular views as it glides over the sea. For a more thrilling experience, you can choose the Crystal Cabin with a transparent floor. On a clear day, you can see as…
Home of Busan's Chinese community with cheap and delicious dumplings, though most of the Chinese have left the area, and it is today mainly home to Russians.
This is an example of old, steep residential area of Busan that was formed after Korean War. Although you can walk the famous 168 steps, there is a free monorail that takes you uphill.

This is a famous lifting bridge that was built in 1934. It was a meeting point for missing families during the Korean War. The current bridge was rebuilt in 2013, and the bridge lifts up at 14:00 for 15 minutes on every Saturday.

Named after King Taejong Muyul (654-661) of the Silla Dynasty who practiced archery here after unifying the Three Kingdoms. During the Joseon period, King Taejong (1400-1418) is reputed to have visited here for recreation and pleasure.…

This was a US military base that was turned into a large park in 2014. The parks have large playground for kids and remnants of military base. The park museum has many artifacts about the history of the US military base and the lives…
Discover the history of Busan from the Prehistoric period to the present day.

This is the only United Nations cemetery in the world. Soldiers from many countries who contributed to the United Nations during the Korean War are buried here. Take bus from in front of the Memorial Park after subway exit. Please note…

If you are interested in the industrial side of Busan then the Port tour is hard to beat. Passengers on board can see the port facilities of Busan Port, including the passenger terminal, general piers, and container terminals. You will…
All-day ticket available for double decker tour buses.

In 2014 a new zoo opened in Busan, with a variety of animals (tigers, lions, bears, elephants, monkeys, etc.) It is very much targeted at children, and there is a very good activity center at the end, with climbing ropes and other…

eat.n: Kim Hee-dae Halmae Wonjo Gamasot Gukbap (Granny Kim Hee-dae's Original Cauldron Gukbap)
eat.b: Gukbap is a hot bowl of rice and broth, and available in many of the old style restaurants in Heaundae market.
Delicious burgers in hand-made bao buns.
A great option if you're craving vegetables. 5 salad choices and a fruit salad for dessert.

Lee Jae-mo Pizza is known as one of Busan’s representative pizza restaurants, so tourists visiting Busan are encouraged to stop by and try the Lee Jae-mo crust pizza. It’s cheaper than other places, and the cheese flavor is excellent,…

eat.n: Subyeon Choe-go Pork Soup, Millak Main Branch
eat.b: There are several chain branches of Subyeon Choegoe Pork Soup, but this is the main branch, so you should go there to enjoy it at its best. The most famous dish is the pork jowl soup with rice, so please be sure to try it.
Hot broths with either chicken or beef cooked with rice and the special Korean ingredient of Ginseng.
Solid Indian fare in a stylish environment.
Really good fish and chips with fresh batter that you can eat outside by the sea. Very long queues on weekends. Also good coffee and ice cream.
Mexican restaurant with a good reputation. Slightly out of the way, but has vegetarian options as well.

eat.n: Busan Etteun Godeungeo – Haeundae Main Branch
eat.b: A Korean restaurant specializing in wood-fired grilled fish, including grilled mackerel and seasoned grilled mackerel. The fish is cooked in a wood-fired oven heated to over 500°C, and the restaurant also offers a self-service bar with…
Novotel Ambassador, Haeundae. Steak, fresh seafood, premier wine. Sephia style interior design, cozy atmosphere, and ocean view.
Decent Italian restaurant at the top of Dalmaji Hill with views over the ocean.
Good if you want some familiar western food.
Nice bakery with good snacks for the beach.
In the basement of a hotel, this is an expensive Korean style booking club.
Pool table and cool Americans aplenty on the weekends. Pretty sleepy during most weeknights.
A chain of bars in Busan and a popular place for Koreans and Westerners to intermingle.

Has live DJs and occasional live bands on weekends. Plays requests during the weekdays. Darts, pool and Hookahs available. Though not busy on most weeknights, there are usually a good mix of foreigners and Koreans inside.
A proper pub serving a large variety of premium draft beers and western food. Great place for a mid week dinner and pint or to party on the weekends. Good mix of Koreans and westerners.

A beloved seafood restaurant and izakaya-style eatery specializing in clams, shellfish, and grilled seafood. It’s a local favorite for late-night dining with cold drinks and lively social atmosphere close to Gwangalli Beach.

A highly rated Korean barbecue restaurant in the Gwangalli area, known for generous portions of grilled meats and quality side dishes. The lively atmosphere and beachside location make it an excellent dinner choice after sightseeing or…
A highly rated casual restaurant focused on salmon and seafood bowls, sushi, and creative fish dishes. Often recommended for seafood lovers looking for a more modern menu near the beach.
A long-established local restaurant serving pork soup, a Busan specialty, often recommended to visitors seeking affordable and authentic regional food.

Busan is famous for raw fish ('회 Hway'), which the Koreans eat in the same style as bulgogi, namely topped with kimchi and gochujang and wrapped in a lettuce leaf. One of the best places to sample this is in a large brown building at…

The owner, Mr. Jun, speaks English, and ordering here is easy: it's either set A, B or C. Even Set A is huge, while C is extremely large. This is as real as it gets and dishes will include still-moving octopus tentacles and other stuff…
A local favorite for fresh sashimi and traditional Korean seafood stews. Known for its high quality and authentic flavors, often featuring seasonal catches.
Plant based Korean food in a quiet setting
A classic Busan-style pork and rice soup. This restaurant is in the Suyeong Gukbap alley and is known for its deep, flavorful broth.
A famous Busan chain specializing in 'Nak-Gop-Sae' (spicy octopus, beef intestine, and shrimp casserole). A hearty and spicy meal, perfect for sharing.
A branch of one of Busan's most famous 'milmyeon' (wheat noodle) restaurants. Offers refreshing cold noodles, both spicy (bibim) and non-spicy (mul).
A humble restaurant near Millak Port serving delicious handmade noodle soup (kalguksu) and pajeon (green onion pancake).
A long-standing local favorite for charcoal-grilled pork ribs (dwaeji galbi). The atmosphere is lively and often packed with locals.
An upscale Italian restaurant with a direct view of the Gwangan Bridge. Specializes in pasta, risotto, and steak.
A popular expatriate-run bar with a friendly atmosphere. Serves excellent Western pub food, including burgers, wings, and fish and chips. Great selection of craft beers.
A popular gourmet burger joint. Known for its juicy, handcrafted patties and fresh ingredients. Often has a line.
A casual New York-style pizzeria selling large slices. A perfect late-night snack to grab and eat by the beach.
A lively Spanish tapas bar serving authentic dishes like gambas al ajillo and paella. Great atmosphere with sangria and wine, plus a good view.
A casual pizza and pub-style restaurant serving pizzas, craft beers, and light dishes. With its beachfront proximity, it’s a popular evening gathering spot for travelers and locals.
A cozy, authentic Japanese izakaya specializing in yakitori (grilled skewers) and various small dishes. Pairs well with sake or beer.
Authentic Thai food restaurant run by a Thai chef. Popular for its Pad Thai and Tom Yum Goong.
A simple, no-frills Vietnamese restaurant serving excellent pho (beef noodle soup) and banh mi. Quick, delicious, and affordable.
Australian-style cafe with variations on brunch and lunch classics.
A very popular cafe on the main beach road, famous for its multi-story glass windows offering unobstructed views of the bridge. Great for coffee and elaborate desserts.
A "newtro" (new-retro) style cafe known for its quiet atmosphere and specialty hand-drip coffee.
A bakery known for its savory breads (like onion or corn bread) and freshly baked goods. A local favorite for breakfast.
A well-known specialty coffee café directly facing Gwangalli Beach, popular with tourists for high-quality coffee and clear views of Gwangan Bridge both during the day and at night.
A premium café brand offering espresso-based drinks in a comfortable setting, often used by tourists as a rest stop while walking along the beachfront.
A popular dessert café known for its donuts and colorful interior, frequently visited by tourists and younger visitors walking along Gwangalli Beach.
‘The Brewery’ is Busan’s first American-style craft beer microbrewery and brewpub.
Serves up gimbap from ₩2000 and all sorts of noodles for ₩2500-4000. No English menu or sign, but if you can say it they'll make it, and it's open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
This food court serves all the usual Korean favorites, with plastic food and English menus making ordering a snap.
Specializes in beef soups and kakkduggi side dish.

European, North American, Russian, and SE Asian dishes; try the borscht stew. Popular with sailors and their lady companions, the best time to go is after midnight. A small shop offering a limited selection of dust-covered western goods…

Turns into a bar, but they serve excellent Western food, and American-style breakfast until the afternoon. Open air bar. Thursday is ladies' bottomless drinks for ₩15000. In-Jung runs the bar and is a great hostess.
Tteokbokki restaurant is inside the can market. Prices are reasonable at ₩5,000 for tteokbokki, ₩5,000 for fries, and ₩1,000 for a corn dog.
Authentic Indian restaurant owned by Indians.

This is the most famous pizza restaurant in Central Busan. On weekdays and weekends, a very large number of people line up to eat inside the restaurant. To solve this problem, a take-out only store has been opened across the street.…

This is a pork cutlet version of the Korean fried chicken called 'Pork Ribs Fried'. It is available in large, medium, and small sizes, with prices ranging from ₩13,000 to ₩23,000 depending on the size.

This Chinese restaurant in Busan, Jung-gu, is famous for its yuni-jjajang and sweet and sour pork. Noodles and fried rice are inexpensive at ₩6,000-8,000, but other dishes cost ₩20,000-30,000. Closed every Wednesday.
It's a Chinese restaurant. Typically, there are regular course meals (₩37,000-85,000 ), lunch course meals (₩23,000-35,000), and couple course meals (₩39,000-49,000), with a 15:30 - 16:30 break.

A Korean barbecue restaurant with a single menu item: beef outside skirt It costs ₩13,000 per bowl and has sides such as Doenjangjjigae, rice, and Naengmyeon. Closed every Sunday and last order is at 21:00.

eat.h: Usually open on Fridays and Saturdays and sometimes throughout the week (although it has been available for rental during the week and Sundays)
eat.b: It's the only place to see regular metal, punk and rock in Busan. A modest amount of beer and booze at the bar is complemented by a selection of in house cocktails. Good place to go and let it all out, scream shout and get wasted and…
In the PNU area you can buy a lot of Korean student food specialties, such as Don Katsu and Croquette (Goroke - 고로케).
A long-running local restaurant specializing in sundae gukbap. Popular among both residents and visitors for its rich broth and generous portions.
A well-known local restaurant specializing in Busan-style pork soup, frequently recommended to visitors seeking an authentic and affordable regional dish.
A traditional Korean restaurant serving loach soup, popular among visitors interested in experiencing regional comfort food near the Nakdong River.
A famous restaurant serving Dongnae-style green onion pancakes, a regional specialty often introduced to tourists as a traditional local dish.
A popular Japanese-style pork cutlet restaurant near Pusan National University. The menu includes loin, tenderloin, Berkshire K pork cutlets, and katsudon.
Thursday Party is a popular pub chain in Korea, and the Pusan National University branch is famous among students for its casual atmosphere, cocktails, and affordable beer.
A classic Dwaeji Gukbap, a pork soup mixed with rice restaurant.
Offers milmyeon (wheat noodles), a regional food item. Both cold noodles (mul milmyeon) and spicy mixed noodles (bibim milmyeon) are available.
Sells tteok-bokki (spicy rice cakes) and eomuk (fish cakes). Provides a typical local street food experience.
Serves seafood rice dishes and grilled fish options. The location provides views of the ocean and the Songdo Marine Cable Car.
Specializes in nakji bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus) and nakgop-sae (octopus, tripe, and shrimp casserole). The dishes are noted for their high spice level.
A cluster of restaurants serving jokbal, a dish of marinated and boiled pig's feet. Various preparations, including cold sliced versions, are available.
Several small vendors and cafes offering quick meals and snacks such as ramyeon (instant noodles), kimbap (seaweed rice rolls), and beverages for sightseers.
Offers hoe (raw fish/sashimi) and seafood sets. The location provides a view of the ocean.
Serves dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), a staple Busan dish. Noted for its rich, clear pork broth.
An all-you-can-eat establishment focusing on grilled clams and shellfish (jogae gui).
